description: The PRG32 audio engine as the firmware implements it: what the Construction Kit's browser runtime, AudioStudio and packager must match. Every value comes from the PRG32 SDK sources named below; tests/test_audio_contract.py checks them against a checkout. docs/audio_engine.md explains them.

voices.kit_policy: The kit builds its engine with exactly 8 voices and its tests fail with fewer. The 6 in audio_config.h applies only to builds without an sdkconfig; it is reported upstream.
voices.explicit_channel: a note or sample on an explicit voice replaces whatever that voice was playing
voices.allocation: prg32_audio_play_sample takes the first inactive voice, else voice 0

output.mix: sum of every active voice, then clamp to -32768..32767 per channel
output.default_mode: stereo (the kit's target is PRG32 Audio Plus); a mono cartridge's mix is written to both channels

volume.voice_then_channel_then_master: pcm = (pcm * voice) >> 8; pcm = (pcm * channel) >> 8; pcm = (pcm * master) >> 9
volume.headroom: the master shift of 9 halves the level (6 dB) so several voices rarely clip

pan.applied: left += pcm * left_gain / 255; right += pcm * right_gain / 255

synth.layout: bit 15 marker; bits 11:10 resonance (0..3); bits 9:6 cutoff (0..15); bits 5:2 pulse width (0..15); bits 1:0 waveform

adsr.time_ms: 0 = immediate; otherwise 1 + v * v * 2000 / 65025 (1 is about 1 ms, 255 about 2001 ms)
adsr.steps: a stage moves the level by a whole step per sample, step = ceil(distance / samples) with samples = sample_rate * ms / 1000, so it lasts ceil(distance / step) samples: a release from a low sustain ends sooner than its nominal time
adsr.note_off: a synth voice enters release; a sample voice stops at once
adsr.release_end: the voice becomes inactive when the level reaches 0
adsr.timed_note: prg32_audio_note(..., duration_ms) releases (synth) or stops (sample) after duration_ms of engine time

tracker.note_on_instrument: a track's NOTE_ON on voice N plays instrument N
tracker.jump_target: arg1 << 8 | arg0; out of range stops the track
tracker.delta_zero: events with delta 0 run in the same tick (a chord)
tracker.delta: an event runs first, then the tracker waits its delta ticks before the next event (audio_tracker.c); the SDK's tools/midi2prg32audio.py writes the MIDI meaning (wait before), an upstream mismatch

block.header_layout: <4sHHHHHHIIIIII: magic, version, header_size, sample_count, instrument_count, track_count, reserved, samples_offset, instruments_offset, tracks_offset, events_offset, data_offset, block_size

sample_desc.layout: <IIIIHBB: offset, length, loop_start, loop_end, base_note, flags, reserved

instrument_desc.layout: <HBbBBBB: sample_id, default_volume, default_pan, attack, decay, sustain, release

block.in_cartridge: after the PRG2 header and code, when the header's AUDIO flag (bit 0) is set; loading it replaces the previous assets after restoring the defaults

abi.blocking: prg32_audio_notes blocks the calling cartridge for the sum of the note durations

legacy_buzzer.firmware: PWM on PRG32_PIN_BUZZER; nothing when the board has no buzzer pin
legacy_buzzer.kit_policy: obsolete and unsupported: never offered (blocks, completions, examples), refused in Advanced C and handwritten assembly with an explanation, and silent in the browser runtime for old cartridges (counted, like a board without a buzzer). Its removal from the SDK's portable ABI is proposed upstream.
